title: Corporate event checklist: from venue to technical rider

coverAlt: Checklist and planning for a corporate event in Podgorica
segments: A corporate event looks effortless only when there is a strong plan behind it. The difference between a corporate event and a regular party is not simply the atmosphere: it is protocol, timing, technical reliability and clearly assigned responsibilities. Attendees may include partners, executives, out-of-town guests and media. Success is measured by whether everything flows smoothly, not just whether people had fun.

In Podgorica, the most common failures happen over basic issues: a presentation that will not run on the projector, a crackling microphone, insufficient power, poor acoustics, a delayed speaker without a contingency plan or a congested entrance without anyone managing arrivals. This checklist is designed to prevent exactly those situations.
1) Venue - before signing

Capacity is more than a number. Ask for seated and standing layouts and check how tables fit around a stage, projection and registration area. Confirm parking and equipment access immediately: logistics can cause more trouble than equipment pricing.

Check acoustics and noise limits. Some visually impressive locations are technically difficult. For outdoor events, require a backup venue or a clear indoor alternative. Most importantly, check electricity: the number and location of sockets and available load. It sounds dull, but poor power planning causes last-minute panic.
2) Programme and protocol

A corporate programme needs an exact schedule. Not 'opening around 7pm', but who speaks, when, for how long, who introduces them, who closes, when Q&A happens and when networking begins. For VIP guests, define arrival, seating, escorts and a responsible contact. VIP protocol should never be improvised.
A practical detail: allow a few minutes between programme blocks. In reality people arrive late, technical transitions take time and a buffer keeps the schedule moving without drama.
3) Technical rider - the essential minimum

Audio: number of handheld and clip microphones, mixing desk, speakers, monitors if speakers need them and the person responsible. Video: projector or LED screen, resolution and adapters. Lighting: basic stage and ambient lighting so speakers do not appear in darkness on camera.
Backup: a spare microphone, batteries, cables and adapters. Schedule the soundcheck and assign an owner. Without a soundcheck, everything seems fine until the first speech starts.
A corporate event runs smoothly only when everyone knows their role and there is one clear point of accountability.
4) Team and responsibilities

A corporate event needs reliable people in key positions. One person should be in overall command. Technicians must be present throughout speeches, not somewhere nearby. If there is registration, hosts at the entrance must know who is expected and what to do if someone is not on the list.

The content team needs its own plan. With photo/video coverage, create a shot list. Otherwise, you get random footage but miss essential moments: speeches, panels, handshakes, branding, audience reactions and networking.
5) Branding and materials

Stage backdrop or logo wall, wayfinding, signs, passes or badges and table materials. Finalize the presentation format: consistent fonts, slide ratios and a backup PDF. It is too common for someone to arrive with a presentation that works only on their laptop. That cannot happen at a professional corporate event.
6) Contingency plan

A backup plan is standard practice, not pessimism. If a speaker is late, have an alternate block ready: networking, a video or a short music break. If equipment fails, have backup audio and PDF presentations. For outdoor events, define the indoor plan in case of rain or wind. Above all, identify the person empowered to decide.
Event-day mini checklist

Venue available for setup on time. Equipment delivered and tested. Soundcheck completed. Presentations tested on the actual equipment. Schedule shared with the team. One person assigned to VIP guests and another to the entrance. Backup PDF ready. Spare microphone and batteries available.
FAQ
What is the most common failure?
An untested presentation and a poor soundcheck. They seem minor but immediately damage the impression.
How early should the team arrive?
Allow 3-6 hours for setup, depending on equipment and branding. For a panel or several speakers, add more rehearsal time.
